name: Tymnes
bio: Tymnes is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 2nd century BC (?). Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of Meleager's Wreath, the Garland compiled about 100 BC.
This archive carries the 5 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 199, 211, 433, 477, 729).

poems.title: Book VII, 199: On an unknown bird called elaeus
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text: Bird, nursling of the Graces, who didst modulate thy voice till it was like unto a halcyon’s, thou art gone, dear elaeus, and the silent ways of night possess thy gentleness and thy sweet breath.

poems.title: Book VII, 211
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text: The stone tells that it contains here the white Maltese dog, Eumelus’ faithful guardian. They called him Bull while he still Jived, but now the silent paths of night possess his voice.

poems.title: Book VII, 433
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text: His Spartan mother slew the Spartan Demetrius for transgressing the law. Bringing her sharp sword to the guard, she said, gnashing her teeth, like a Laconian woman as she was: “Perish, craven whelp, evil piece, to Hell with thee! He who is not worthy of Sparta is not my son.”

poems.title: Book VII, 477
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text: Let not this, Philaenis, weigh on thy heart, that the earth in which it was thy fate to lie is not beside the Nile, but that thou art laid in this tomb at Eleutherna. From no matter where the road is the same to Hades.

poems.title: Book VII, 729
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text: The omens were evil when fair Tritonis was brought to bed, for otherwise she would not have perished, unhappy girl, just after the child was born. With her this one babe brought down to Hades so much happiness, and it did not even live beyond the tenth dawn.

poems.title: Book XVI, 237: On the Same
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text: I behave like Priapus to everyone, even be he Cronos, so little distinction do I make between thieves here beside this kitchen-garden. Someone will tell me it is not meet for me to say this for the sake of greens and pumpkins. It is not meet, but I say it.
